clue.text: Merely leaves the army, but gets one's comeuppance

parts.note: merely means just, as in 'just a minute'
a soldier who leaves the army without permission deserts

explanation.surface: A soldier who simply walks away from service ends up getting punished for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A comeuppance is the punishment someone has earned, which is what they deserve.

clue.text: Boss shows hesitation taking on backward ex-pupil

parts.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating

indicators.note: backward tells us the letters for the ex-pupil are read from the end

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: A headteacher dithers when taking on a former pupil who is a bit slow.
explanation.walkthrough: The boss here is not an employer but the raised centre of a shield; 'backward' gives BO, after the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised knob at the centre of a shield is called its boss, a technical sense.

clue.text: Storm when MEP is ordered to appear in trial

indicators.note: the rearranged politician's letters must turn up inside the word for trial

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the three letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A Euro MP is summoned to stand trial in court.
explanation.walkthrough: The storm is no political row: 'ordered' gives EMP, which 'to appear in' places within the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent storm, as in Shakespeare's play title.

clue.text: Prior to climb Sicilian mount

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ante is Latin for before, prior to

explanation.surface: Instructions to climb before reaching the summit of a mountain in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climb' in a down entry turns ANTE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a mountain there.

clue.text: Set teas served in stately homes

indicators.note: served suggests something laid out in a new arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Afternoon tea is laid on for visitors to grand country houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' rearranges SETTEAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Large country houses with their land are known as estates.

clue.text: Excessively large instrument

parts.note: too means excessively, as in 'too hot'
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A description of an oversized implement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool is an implement or instrument used for a task.

clue.text: Senseless babble from look-alike wife

parts.note: a double is someone who looks just like another
'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for one's wife

explanation.surface: Someone talks nonsense after meeting a woman who resembles his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: DUTCH for wife comes from Cockney 'my old Dutch' (from duchess), a London East End expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Dutch is an idiom for incomprehensible talk or gibberish.

clue.text: Form an ambition to conceal love. It's anathema

indicators.note: concealing means hiding something inside, so one piece goes within the other
form means to shape anew, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: Advice to develop a goal while hiding affection, which is said to be detestable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' rearranges ANAMBITION, and 'to conceal' puts O inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something anathema is utterly detested, which is what an abomination is.

clue.text: Socially ubiquitous whatever occurs

explanation.surface: A party animal who turns up everywhere, whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is playful: someone present at all the social events.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the phrase means attending every function; as an idiom it means in any case, whatever happens.

clue.text: English acquired one in state diplomacy

indicators.note: in tells us the three pieces sit inside the word for state

parts.note: a nation is a state
got means acquired
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Englishman gets a single post in a country's diplomatic service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EGOTI inside NATION, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Diplomacy is the art of discussion and bargaining between parties to reach agreement.

clue.text: 50% attend Edward's lecture with little enthusiasm

parts.note: 50 per cent is a half
to hear a case is to attend to it, as a judge does
Ted is short for Edward, and a TED talk is a famous kind of lecture

explanation.surface: Only half the audience turns up for Edward's talk, showing little interest.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something half-heartedly means doing it without real commitment or zeal.

clue.text: German king unaffected by reversals

indicators.note: a name that stays the same when read backwards is untouched by turning it round

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A German monarch who never changes his mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The name reads the same in both directions, so reversing it changes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Several medieval German kings and Holy Roman Emperors bore this name, such as the Great.

clue.text: Taken to a Spartan queen

parts.note: taken somewhere means led there

explanation.surface: Someone is escorted into the presence of a queen of Sparta.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth she was wife of King Tyndareus of Sparta, seduced by Zeus as a swan.

clue.text: Aggregate and aluminium found in dynamite

indicators.note: found in says one piece is located inside the other

parts.note: dynamite produces a blast, an explosion
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A list of materials: crushed stone and metal discovered in explosives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aggregate' looks like a verb but means crushed stone; 'found in' places the metal inside the explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ballast is crushed stone or gravel used as a base for railway tracks, a kind of aggregate.

clue.text: Conditions during periods of schooling

explanation.surface: Rules that apply while children are at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Terms are the conditions of an agreement, and also the divisions of the school year.

clue.text: Anticipate the Red Queen's order

explanation.surface: Foreseeing what the fierce queen in the story will command.
explanation.walkthrough: The queen's famous cry is 'Off with her head!', so her order is to take a head off.
explanation.definitionFit: To forestall or intercept something is to anticipate it; the queen's repeated command was to have a head removed.

clue.text: Custom-made costume

explanation.surface: Clothing tailored to order.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'custom-made' as one phrase; split, 'Custom' is one definition and 'made' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a usual practice or custom, and also a distinctive garment such as a nun's or a riding outfit.

clue.text: Meals taken round ten in the States

indicators.note: round says the letters for meals are placed around the other piece

parts.note: teas are light afternoon or evening meals in Britain
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Dinners served at about ten o'clock in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts X inside TEAS. The definition names a place found in the States: one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty US states, so it lies within America.

clue.text: They look for sounds of agreement

indicators.note: sounds of says the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: ayes are votes of agreement in a parliament

explanation.surface: Searching for murmurs of assent in a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounds of' points to AYES spoken aloud.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of sight are what do the looking.

clue.text: Jack and I have a dance

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in cards
've is the contracted form of have, as in I've

explanation.surface: A man named Jack and the speaker enjoy a dance together.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive is a lively style of dance to swing or rock and roll music.

clue.text: Scope for a medic with sex appeal

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, from the 1920s 'It girl'

explanation.surface: Room for a doctor who is attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means the range or extent of something, its scope.

clue.text: Tired as can be when mounted on a horse

indicators.note: can be suggests the letters may take another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rider who is as exhausted as anyone could be while in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges TIREDAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on either side is how a rider sits on a horse.

clue.text: Gladiatorial weapon to be deployed in nuclear warfare

explanation.surface: A three-pronged spear from the arena reused for atomic war.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is also the name of the UK's submarine-launched nuclear missile system.
explanation.definitionFit: The retiarius gladiator fought with a three-pronged spear and net; the same name was given to a nuclear missile.

clue.text: Sue's disposed to embrace Leslie, but in vain

indicators.note: embracing means holding in the arms, so one piece goes inside the other
disposed means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Sue with the S of its possessive
Les is the short form of Leslie

explanation.surface: Sue wants to hug Leslie, but her efforts come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Leslie is shortened as usual; 'disposed' gives USES and 'to embrace' wraps that round him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done to no avail or without result is futile.

clue.text: Characteristic otherwise exhibited by Judas

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry, or you'll be late'

explanation.surface: A distinctive quality otherwise displayed by the disciple Judas.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas betrayed Jesus, so his name stands for a betrayer.

clue.text: Pretty shrewd

explanation.surface: Rather clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Cute means attractive, and also sharp or clever in a crafty way.

clue.text: Record written on Early English sword

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
EE is the abbreviation for Early English, a style of architecture

explanation.surface: Something recorded on an old English blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing weapon, a light thrusting blade.

clue.text: It's up to a king to create revolution

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the letters of the word as written, ignoring the apostrophe
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: It is the monarch's decision whether to start an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests a rebellion but means commotion; 'up' gives STI before the king.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir is to agitate or provoke unrest, stirring things up.

clue.text: Rushed to get rent

explanation.surface: Hurried to collect the money owed by a tenant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' is not the tenant's payment but the past tense of rend.
explanation.definitionFit: Tore means dashed headlong, and also ripped apart, the past tense of tear.

clue.text: Drive the car around and go

explanation.surface: Telling a driver to swing the vehicle round and leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Turning means bringing a car round to face another way; a turn is also one's go in a game.

clue.text: Foul pint he's brewed may mar one's enjoyment

indicators.note: brewed means concocted, so the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A nasty pint of home brew could ruin a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges FOULPINTHES.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin a pleasurable occasion for others is to dampen their pleasure.

clue.text: Perceptive writer needs extra-terrestrial assessment

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
ET is the abbreviation for extra-terrestrial, as in the film
a rating is an assessment

explanation.surface: An author requires an alien's evaluation.
explanation.definitionFit: A penetrating mind sees deeply into things, being sharply insightful.
